db_evidence.notes: The true shrine visit spans roughly 63367-63630s. The on-screen shrine title '火燎一关' (Fire Scorch stage 1) and the click on 铸造 (Forging) are directly visible starting at ~63367-63383s (confirmed by manually pulled frames), squarely inside the given clue_interval. However, the 30-second episode captions in this window never mention '火燎'/'Fire Scorch'/'土地庙' by name -- episodes:30sec:002113 (63390-63420) only describes 'a dark shrine menu with two flaming sword-pillars and options such as 消息, 领地, 修行, 铸造, 货殖, 赠礼, 炼开, and 离开' (which does include 货殖/Commerce, matching the reference answer), so a plain run_sql range query CAN surface the right row (rollout-01 did this), but semantic_search on the literal phrase 'Fire Scorch'/'火燎'/'土地庙' does not reliably hit it, and clip_qa calls anchored on a later part of the same extended shrine visit (63500-63630s) saw a reordered/updated menu list (调息, 缩地, 修行, 铸造, 泡制, 赏组, 炼丹, 离开 -- missing 货殖) that looks like a different, confusable instance. A visually near-identical but distinct 'stage 3' shrine visit ('火燎三关') exists later at ~71130-71200s and repeatedly drew agents' searches and clip_qa calls away from the true stage-1 clue.

root_causes: Multiple near-duplicate, similarly-labeled shrine visits exist in the video ('火燎一关' stage 1 at ~63400s vs '火燎三关' stage 3 at ~71150s); 3 of 5 rollouts (00, 02, and partially 01) confused stage 3 for stage 1 because both are thematically and visually similar 'fire scorch shrine menu' scenes

2 of 5 rollouts (03, 04) misinterpreted 'first time' as the earliest literal on-screen/narrative mention of the string '土地庙' in the whole video (~2820-3690s, a narrative/dialogue marker), rather than the actual gameplay moment when the shrine's level-1 menu is opened and clicked

The 30-second episode/event captions around the true clue window never literally say 'Fire Scorch' or the shrine's on-screen title, so keyword-oriented semantic_search queries for 'Fire Scorch'/'火燎'/'土地庙' systematically failed to rank the true clue interval highly, even though a raw run_sql time-range query (rollout-01) did surface it

what_worked: Rollout-01's run_sql time-range query (episodes BETWEEN 63300 AND 63840) did retrieve the ground-truth episode row describing the correct shrine menu (including 货殖/Commerce), showing that a broad SQL time-window scan around the given clue_interval can surface the right evidence even when keyword search fails
clip_qa correctly read the on-screen Chinese shrine title '火燎一关' when pointed at frames within the right shrine visit (rollout-01), confirming OCR-level visual grounding was working
transferable_lessons: When a question names a specific numbered/staged location (e.g. 'first stage'), explicitly check for and disambiguate near-duplicate later-stage instances (e.g. a 'stage 3' shrine with a similar name) before committing to a clip_qa window -- don't rely on semantic similarity alone to distinguish 'stage 1' from 'stage 3'

'First time X happened' should be resolved by finding the first occurrence of the actual event/action described (e.g. the shrine menu being opened and options clicked), not the first literal mention of a keyword/place-name elsewhere in the video (e.g. an unrelated narrative/dialogue screen using the same string)

When semantic_search on a literal phrase from the question (e.g. 'Fire Scorch', '土地庙') returns weak or no hits near the given clue_interval, fall back to a plain run_sql time-range scan centered on total_intervals/clue_interval -- captions may describe the same on-screen content without ever using the question's wording

When clip_qa inspects a scene, always include the very start of the given clue_interval, not just a nearby or slightly later window; menu state can visibly change (items reordered, added, removed) within tens of seconds, and 'what's highlighted now' at a later slice is not the same as 'what was clicked at the start'

Distinguish a highlighted/hovered menu item from an actually-confirmed click by looking for the transition into the resulting submenu/screen (e.g. 铸造 expanding into 兵器铸造/披挂铸造 and then an equipment-forging screen), not just cursor position in a single frame
